data.name: Lauresse Regency
data.short_lore: Lauresse was once the most chivalric crown on the continent, its knights sworn to castles on every hill. Now the sickly child-king Sanhel lies in Ysembert while three regents bicker over a treasury that is empty, its granaries mortgaged to river bankers in Pellegrane. Fen raiders strike Ondrac's causeways unanswered, and every lord keeps his levies at home.

towns.name: Corbanel
towns.blurb: Wine-cellar town; the crown's last unpawned casks sleep under its market hall.

towns.name: Ondrac
towns.blurb: Causeway town on the marsh edge, famous for its toll-gates and the grudge of Fen raids.

towns.name: Tessaguel
towns.blurb: Cloth market where dyed silks fetch lordly prices, and where guild factors count the regents' debts.

towns.name: Brisamont
towns.blurb: Hill-fort town with the realm's oldest tourney field and a legend of a dead king's horn.

towns.name: Pellegrane
towns.blurb: Pilgrim-road town holding the mortgage deeds on half the royal granaries, owed to river bankers.

towns.name: Mordelle
towns.blurb: Border town of wool and gallows, where rival regent banners hang side by side and never stop feuding.

castles.name: Castelnarc
castles.blurb: Largest keep in the realm; its walls still bear the scorch marks of the Regents' War.

castles.name: Ysembert
castles.blurb: Sickroom fortress where the child-king sleeps under a dozen physicians' watchful eyes.

castles.name: Montsorel
castles.blurb: Hilltop castle whose lord claims the regency by right of his mother's blood.

castles.name: Nerveille
castles.blurb: Marshland castle guarding the causeway; its garrison is paid late and its keeper is often drunk.

castles.name: Garrouse
castles.blurb: Mountain keep with a gate of black oak and a legend of a knight who never came down.

castles.name: Ombrelac
castles.blurb: Lakeside castle whose moat is said to hold the drowned crowns of old kings.

castles.name: Seguiral
castles.blurb: Abbey-castle famous for its wall tapestries, sold piece by piece to pay mercenary wages.

castles.name: Tourbelle
castles.blurb: Tower-castle of the eastern march, where lords refuse to send levies beyond their own borders.

castles.name: Ravinesse
castles.blurb: Cliffside castle whose lord turned coat three times in one summer; no one trusts his banner.

villages.name: Auberrac
villages.blurb: Vineyard hamlet with a famous sour red that soldiers drink before every battle.

villages.name: Pichelle
villages.blurb: Mill village whose waterwheel is the regency's only dependable tax income.

villages.name: Sanquerec
villages.blurb: Chapel village where a miracle spring is said to cure the ailing king's fever.

villages.name: Ganteil
villages.blurb: Shepherd village known for glove-makers and a long feud with the nearby lord's pigs.

villages.name: Roucalh
villages.blurb: Quarry village supplying the great castles; its stonemasons strike whenever pay is late.

villages.name: Vignebel
villages.blurb: Orchard village; its cider is served at every regent's feast and blamed for every quarrel.

villages.name: Lorgesse
villages.blurb: Ferry village where river-guild toll-men and royal sergeants trade insults every day.

villages.name: Dusmerc
villages.blurb: Forest-edge village of charcoal burners who sell to whichever lord pays first.

villages.name: Fontagne
villages.blurb: Spring village with a stone well carved with the old kings' names, half scratched out.

villages.name: Cazelune
villages.blurb: Hunting village where the regents hold tournaments to prove which of them is bravest.

villages.name: Brenvaud
villages.blurb: Bridge village guarding the only dry crossing; its lord has never paid a toll himself.

villages.name: Aurigol
villages.blurb: Gold-dust village whose miners are paid in promissory notes from the empty treasury.

villages.name: Teoulac
villages.blurb: Fishing village on a mere; locals claim a drowned knight rings the bell at night.

villages.name: Ymbrane
villages.blurb: Hill village known for falconers, whose hawks are gifts exchanged between rival lords.

villages.name: Sauvanesse
villages.blurb: Monastery village whose scribes keep the realm's genealogies, and forge them when needed.

villages.name: Quelmont
villages.blurb: Quiet hamlet of salt-pan workers, fighting the river-guild over every bag they sell.

villages.name: Bertrevol
villages.blurb: Pasture village whose sheep are the last reliable wool bond left to the crown.

villages.name: Mezeroc
villages.blurb: Stone bridge village where a lord's murder in the reeds still goes unsolved.

villages.name: Oulhac
villages.blurb: Iron-smithing village whose forges melt down old banners to make pikeheads.

villages.name: Presquel
villages.blurb: Orchard village beside a ruined manor; its heir is the child-king's rival for the crown.

villages.name: Serrandol
villages.blurb: Ridge village with a watchtower that signals the border; its beacon is lit far too often.
